title: Small free finite-coproduct envelope and coherent extension of diagrams
statement:
Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], with small meaning $\mathcal U$-small, and simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A finite coproduct means a colimit of a diagram indexed by a finite discrete simplicial set, with the empty diagram included; preservation means sending every such colimiting cocone to a colimiting cocone. For every small simplicial set $K$ there exist a small quasicategory $J$ admitting finite coproducts, including an initial object, and a simplicial map $i:K\to J$ with the following properties. Every object of $J$ is equivalent to a finite coproduct of vertices $i(k)$, with the empty coproduct allowed. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in the larger universe which admits finite coproducts, and every coherent diagram $F:K\to\mathcal E$, there exist a coherent functor $\widehat F:J\to\mathcal E$ preserving finite coproducts and a coherent equivalence $\eta:F\simeq\widehat F i$. For every coherent functor $H:J\to\mathcal E$, restriction followed by precomposition with $\eta$ is an equivalence of whole mapping spaces
$$
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\widehat F,H)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(F,Hi),\qquad t\longmapsto (ti)\eta,
$$
naturally in $H$, including all higher simplices. No preservation property is required of $H$, and no local smallness, accessibility or cocompleteness is assumed of $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Remark 5.3.5.9 (free completion under finite coproducts, with its left Kan extension property); Proposition 5.3.6.2 for the completion universal property; Section 4.3.2 for left Kan extensions. The arbitrary simplicial-set version passes first to a small categorical fibrant replacement. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical construction.

proof.text: Work in the universes of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], with the coherent conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] to the coherent realization $\mathfrak C[K]$ and its object-preserving locally Kan replacement $A=R\mathfrak C[K]$. The objects of $\mathfrak C[K]$ are precisely $K_0$: in its simplex-colimit construction the vertices are identified exactly by the simplicial identifications defining $K_0$. Thus $A$ has object set $K_0$ and remains small. Put $B=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$. The adjoint $q:K\to B$ of $\mathfrak C[K]\to A$ is a Joyal equivalence: all simplicial sets are cofibrant, $A$ is fibrant, and the Quillen-equivalence criterion applied to this replacement weak equivalence gives the assertion. The same cited node makes $B$ a small quasicategory. By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], $q^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ is a coherent functor equivalence for every allowed target. In particular, a given $F$ has a lift $F_0:B\to\mathcal E$ with a specified coherent equivalence $\eta:F\simeq F_0q$.

source.place: Section 1.1.5; Theorem 2.2.5.1 (coherent realization/nerve Quillen equivalence). Explicit reduction of arbitrary K, not an assertion made in Remark 5.3.5.9.

proof.text:
Define a simplicial category $D$ with objects the finite lists $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ of objects of $A$, including $m=0$, and
$$D(a,b)=\coprod_{\phi:[m]\to[n]}\prod_{r=1}^m A(a_r,b_{\phi(r)}),\qquad b=(b_1,\ldots,b_n).$$
The index sets here are $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Define $(\psi,(g_s))\circ(\phi,(f_r))=(\psi\phi,(g_{\phi(r)}f_r)_r)$ and identities by identity functions and identity arrows. The associativity and unit equations are those in $A$, coordinate by coordinate; simplicial operators act on each $f_r$. Products and disjoint unions of Kan complexes are Kan: fill each product coordinate, and for a horn in a disjoint union its connected nonempty domain lies in one summand. All these sets are small. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], $J=N_{\mathrm{hc}}D$ is small and its mapping spaces are naturally equivalent to $D(a,b)$, compatibly with composition. Singleton lists identify $B$ with a full subcategory of $J$, since a simplex all of whose vertices are singleton lists has exactly the coherent data of a simplex in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$. Denote the inclusion by $e$ and put $i=eq$. Concatenation $a^{(1)}\mathbin{\|}\cdots\mathbin{\|}a^{(r)}$ has inclusion arrows given by the index injections and identity components. Restriction along them gives the simplicial isomorphism
$$D(a^{(1)}\mathbin{\|}\cdots\mathbin{\|}a^{(r)},b)\cong\prod_{s=1}^rD(a^{(s)},b).$$
It groups a function and its component arrows by its source blocks; its inverse concatenates those data. For $r=0$ this is the one-point space. The mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore proves these are coproduct cocones in $J$, including the initial empty list. Every list is the coproduct of its singleton entries, which are images of vertices of $K$.

source.place: Remark 5.3.5.9 and Proposition 5.3.6.2, finite-discrete-shape case; explicit small finite-family model supplied here. The nerve and mapping-space comparisons use Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 2.2.4.1.

proof.text:
Fix $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in J$ and put $T_a=B\times_J J_{/a}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] this is a right fibration over $B$. The mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and the singleton-source instance of the displayed formula give a natural equivalence of presheaves on $B$,
$$\coprod_{r=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_B(-,a_r)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_J(e(-),a).$$
Its $r$th map is postcomposition with the $r$th singleton inclusion $e(a_r)\to a$: the composition compatibility in the cited comparison identifies it with inclusion of that summand of $D((b),a)$. By the right-fibration classification and slice compatibility of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], these presheaves classify respectively $\coprod_r B_{/a_r}\to B$ and $T_a\to B$. For the first assertion, disjoint union of these right fibrations is a right fibration, with the disjoint union of their fibers and componentwise transport. Consequently the natural map induced by the singleton inclusions is an equivalence over $B$,
$$v_a:\coprod_{r=1}^m B_{/a_r}\simeq T_a.$$
On each component it sends $(b\to a_r)$ to its composite $e(b)\to e(a_r)\to a$, with the corresponding coherent simplices. For $m=0$ both sides are empty: the presheaf in question is everywhere empty. This proves a decomposition into slices, not an identification of $T_a$ with a finite discrete category.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Section 2.2.4, applied to the finite-family mapping formula; explicit comma-category calculation for the finite-coproduct case of Remark 5.3.5.9.

proof.text: For each $r$, the identity arrow of $a_r$ is final in $B_{/a_r}$ by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] to the diagram $B_{/a_r}\to B\xrightarrow{F_0}\mathcal E$: its colimit is $F_0(a_r)$, with the identity leg at that final object. Put $L_a=\coprod_{r=1}^m F_0(a_r)$, using only the assumed finite coproducts in $\mathcal E$. The component cocones followed by the coproduct legs give a colimiting cocone on $\coprod_r B_{/a_r}$. Explicitly, for every $z$ the space of cocones with apex $z$ is the product over $r$ of the component cocone spaces, since a transformation on a disjoint union is exactly one transformation on each component, in every simplicial degree. The cited final-object colimit property identifies this product with $\prod_r\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F_0(a_r),z)$, and the coproduct universal property identifies it with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L_a,z)$. The cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves the claim. Precomposition by the equivalence $v_a$ of step 3 gives equivalences of functor and cocone categories: precomposing with its coherent quasi-inverse gives an inverse, and the two natural equivalences give the unit and counit after precomposition. Thus the diagram $T_a\to B\xrightarrow{F_0}\mathcal E$ has a colimit. For the empty list the cocone space is a point, and $L_a$ is initial. The same computation shows that restriction from a $T_a$-cocone to its $m$ singleton-summand legs identifies its cocone space with $\prod_r\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F_0(a_r),z)$.

source.place: Section 4.3.2, pointwise colimit condition; finite-discrete-shape specialization of Remark 5.3.5.9. Final-object evaluation also Kerodon Example 7.2.1.4 (03LQ) and Proposition 4.7.3.20 (02J2), carried by the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: The unique map $p:\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration in the sense specified by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence]: its inner-horn lifting problems are the quasicategory horn-filling problems in $\mathcal E$, and the unique base equivalence is the identity, lifted at any prescribed source by its identity edge.

source.place: Relative Kan application over the terminal base; terminal projection verification.

proof.text: For each $T_a$, step 4 gives a coherent colimiting cocone with apex $L_a$. The fixed-boundary, fixed-apex fiber equivalence in [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] supplies a join cocone $q_a:T_a^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$, with exactly that boundary and apex, whose coherent cocone is equivalent to the chosen one. It is colimiting by the mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For $p:\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$, both lower spaces of the square in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] are points. Thus its homotopy-pullback test says exactly that the upper map is an equivalence, which is the coherent cocone criterion. Consequently $q_a$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] to the full subcategory $B\subseteq J$, $h=F_0$, this $p$, and $s:J\to\Delta^0$. The base equalities are automatic. It yields $\widehat F:J\to\mathcal E$ restricting exactly to $F_0$, whose canonical $T_a$ join cocones are $p$-colimits. The same constant-test and coherent cocone criteria show that their associated coherent cocones are colimiting.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, over the terminal base, with the finite-family local colimits computed in steps 3-4; HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15. Coherent assembly is supplied by this theorem, not by choosing objectwise coproducts.

proof.text: Step 4 identifies restriction of a $T_a$-cocone to its singleton-summand legs with $\prod_r\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F_0(a_r),z)$. Apply this to the canonical colimiting cocone from the preceding step. The cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] shows that its actual legs $F_0(a_r)\to\widehat F(a)$ exhibit $\widehat F(a)$ as their coproduct. In particular the empty list maps to an initial object.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, over the terminal base, with the finite-family local colimits computed in steps 3-4; HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15. Coherent assembly is supplied by this theorem, not by choosing objectwise coproducts.

proof.text: For finitely many lists $a^{(s)}$, let $a$ be their concatenation. Use [lem-coef-finite-coproduct-regrouping] with $x_{sr}=F_0(a^{(s)}_r)$, $y_s=\widehat F(a^{(s)})$ and $z=\widehat F(a)$. The preceding step gives the block coproducts and the coproduct on all singleton entries. The inclusion of an entry into its block followed by the block inclusion is its concatenation inclusion; the functor $\widehat F$ carries this composition triangle to the required coherent triangle in $\mathcal E$. The regrouping lemma therefore proves that the images of the block inclusions are a coproduct cocone. Its empty-family clause includes the empty concatenation.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, over the terminal base, with the finite-family local colimits computed in steps 3-4; HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15. Coherent assembly is supplied by this theorem, not by choosing objectwise coproducts.

proof.text: For any fixed finite family in $J$, the concatenation cocone and every other coproduct cocone are initial objects of the same coherent cocone category. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], its initial-object subcategory is a contractible Kan complex, so these cocones are equivalent with the boundary family fixed. Applying $\widehat F$ sends an equivalence and its inverse witnesses to an equivalence of image cocones. The image of the concatenation cocone is colimiting by the preceding step; the mapping-space criterion of the same cited node shows that a cocone equivalent to it is colimiting as well. Thus $\widehat F$ preserves every finite coproduct cocone. Take the equivalence $\eta:F\simeq F_0q=\widehat F i$ from step 1. Only the finite coproducts and the slice colimits of step 4 have been used.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, over the terminal base, with the finite-family local colimits computed in steps 3-4; HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15. Coherent assembly is supplied by this theorem, not by choosing objectwise coproducts.

proof.text:
For every coherent $H:J\to\mathcal E$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] with $\mathcal C=J$, $\mathcal A=B$, $F=\widehat F$ and $G=H$. Its left Kan hypothesis is exactly the colimiting canonical $T_a$-cocones obtained in step 6. Restriction itself therefore gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\widehat F,H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)}(F_0,He).$$
Precomposition by $q$ is a coherent functor equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], so it induces equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. It identifies the right side with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(F_0q,Hi)$. Precomposition with the fixed equivalence $\eta:F\simeq F_0q$ then gives the required target space; composition with an inverse of $\eta$ is its inverse up to the coherent inverse equations. The composite comparison is precisely $t\mapsto(ti)\eta$. The first comparison is natural restriction by its cited statement, and precomposition by $q$ and $\eta$ commutes with postcomposition in $H$, with the coherent composition homotopies. Hence the specified map is natural in $H$ on whole mapping spaces, retaining their higher simplices. No coproduct preservation of $H$ has entered any hypothesis.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.6.9; HTT Proposition 4.3.2.17. Transport across the specified q and eta is written explicitly.
